correctness.rationale: For independent homogeneous Poisson intensities 1 and ε, expected richness is S=2−exp(−x)−exp(−εx) and elasticity z=xS′/S. Independently differentiated to H=S P−x(SQ+P²) and used symbolic algebra to verify exactly the three-term decomposition with p=e^(−x), q=e^(−εx), y=εx. Its denominator S² is strictly positive. The proof covers the entire x>0 domain in four complementary pieces: small x, early-to-transition x≈L+logL, long positive middle interval, and late tail x≈y*/ε to infinity. Early centered limit H/ε→1−e^(−u) and derivative→e^(−u) gives one simple minimum; late H/ε→e^(−y)[2(1−y)−e^(−y)] gives one simple maximum because the bracket strictly decreases. Uniform exponential bounds rule out other zeros between and after. Independent symbolic derivative and four progressively smaller ε tests reproduced x−, y*, z heights. The limit is explicitly only ε sufficiently small, not all ε.

value.rationale: PASS: the familiar two-species Poisson richness law has a delicate three-scale elasticity profile, requiring global zero exclusion and two different asymptotic coordinates. The sharp location/height transition is a natural interpretable species–area invariant and not the mere observation that rare species affect larger surveyed areas. It is not extrapolated to empirical heterogeneity.
